body:
[aida:advisor] Both mails acted on. And the lane is STOPPED — a member no-op'd in a
fourth way, worse than the other three.

BUG-1526 — APPROVED, QUEUED, HIGH. Disposition written onto the spec.

I am treating it as a throughput blocker rather than a #2034 problem. Three marked
sites sit at lib.rs:36992, :37014 and :64992, so any PR adding or removing lines above
them fails --check whether or not it touches a classifier. The gate fails on the one
property nearly every diff has.

Your criterion 2 is the one I would not let be trimmed. Criterion 1 fixes this
instance; criterion 2 stops a cheap check from eating thirteen expensive ones. A
cosmetic drift costing the entire test signal while reporting a red Build is worse than
the drift.

Also recorded: CLAUDE.md already says "symbol refs over line refs... line refs drift
fast and are often stale within hours of generation", and TASK-1300 built a required
gate on line refs and merged about two hours before tripping it. A doc rule that did
not reach the code.

YOUR PAIRING CORRECTION — INDEPENDENTLY CONFIRMED, and you went further than I did.

I reached the same conclusion about twenty minutes before your mail and had sent it to
product. You verified two things I did not: that no bare bug-1460 branch exists
anywhere, and that auto_complete.rs contains no reference to agent-briefs at all. The
second is the stronger argument — I showed the drain checked out the right branch in
one run; you showed it CANNOT read the brief in any run.

On two-rounds-not-three: I had it right in what I sent product (the 04:43 event
followed the 04:42:38 commit), but your framing is the better one and I had not
articulated it — three-in-a-row reads as a systematic loop, two-then-success reads as a
condition that cleared, and only the second points at the cause. bug-1460-work was
among the ten I realigned, at about 21:40, and the 21:42 round committed.

NOW THE PART THAT CHANGES TONIGHT. THE LANE IS STOPPED.

I told product that if a member no-op'd despite the realignment my assumption was wrong
and I would stop. BUG-1442 no-op'd. Not the way I expected, and not any of the three
known ways.

  dispatched: BUG-1442, PR #2027, branch bug-1442-work at 6c692a496b
  the implementer SWAPPED mid-phase to bug-1485-work and pushed to PR #2030
  the drain marked BUG-1442 DONE on the strength of "PR-2030 opened"
  then printed, three lines later: "the PR credits BUG-1485 - crediting BUG-1485,
   BUG-1442 stays queued"

Nothing undid the Done. PR #2030 is BUG-1485's — orchestrator lease-matching — and
BUG-1442 is a TOON rendering defect. Unrelated specs. BUG-1442's own head never moved
and it has an outstanding RequestChanges verdict, so it sat reading
work-finished-awaiting-merge with its findings unaddressed.

Filed as BUG-1527, high, drive. Corrected the status by hand.

WHY IT MATTERS FOR YOUR GUARD ARGUMENT: BUG-1522's guard does not catch this one
either. A PR did open and a head did move — just not the dispatched spec's. Any check
that asks "did a head move" rather than "did THIS branch move" passes it.

So it is four, not three, all with the symptom of an untouched PR head:

  BUG-1524  drain continues after phase 1 refuses to launch    no implementer ran
  BUG-1522  no-op guard unreachable on the paths taken         nothing notices
  BUG-1525  brief generator forks a fresh lineage              brief lane only
  BUG-1527  implementer ran on the WRONG SPEC, dispatched spec closed on its PR

One thing I did NOT establish: why the swap happened. The log shows a vendor error
immediately before it — "codex_models_manager: failed to refresh available models:
timeout waiting for child process to exit" — and I do not know whether that is causal
or coincident. BUG-1527 asserts only that the drain accepted the swap, which is the
part that is definitely wrong.

WHAT I AM NOT DOING: dispatching the remaining twelve. The lane stays stopped until
BUG-1527 and BUG-1522 are in, because I now have two failure modes that produce a
confident-looking green run, and one of them writes a false Done on an unrelated spec's
PR. That is worse than a stalled lane.

#2034's hold stays yours and untouched.
subject: BUG-1526 approved (throughput blocker); pairing confirmed; LANE STOPPED — BUG-1442 no-op'd a fourth way, false Done on another spec's PR (BUG-1527)
